3-day trip: approach day, summit day (round trip from camp), exit day

contradictions.fact: Summit-day start time and duration

claims.says: 3:30 AM from camp
3:30 AM Leave high camp ... 1:00 PM Back at high camp (9.5 hours elapsed)
guided parties budget 5-7 hours to high camp and another 3-5 hours (6-9 hours total on summit day) from camp to the top
...before this objective ... the 5.5-hr, 05:00-start summit push
...on top of a 5.5-hr summit day

contradictions.why: Five different figures describe the same summit day: 7 hrs (timing/itinerary field), 9.5 hrs (the itinerary's own timestamped schedule, 3:30 AM to 1:00 PM), 6-9 hrs (approach prose), and 5.5 hrs starting at 05:00 (partner_requirements) — the last of which also disagrees with the 3:30 AM start stated everywhere else.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The itinerary's own schedule (3:30 AM-1:00 PM = 9.5 hrs) is the most granular and self-consistent; the '7' hours field in the same day object and the 5.5-hr/05:00 partner_requirements figures both undercount it.

contradictions.fact: Approach text describes summiting Eldorado Peak, not Tepeh Towers

claims.says: From camp, the route continues onto glaciated terrain (roped travel and crevasse-rescue gear required) climbing toward Eldorado's famous narrow snow ridge and the 8,868-foot summit, typically another 3-5 hours.
IMPORTANT — this route is NOT on Eldorado Peak itself, despite being filed under the same area... Tepeh Towers are passed along this same glacier traverse
Tepeh Towers, elevFt absent, elev 8113

contradictions.why: The main body of the approach field is copy-pasted from the Eldorado East Ridge route and describes climbing to Eldorado's 8,868-ft summit via its snow ridge — a different climb entirely from Tepeh Towers' actual one-pitch 5.0 route to 8,113 ft — and is only caught by a caveat appended at the end of the same field.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own high_point_ft (8113), summit waypoint, pitch_detail (1 pitch, 5.0), and the field's own trailing disclaimer show the contaminated first part of 'approach' is wrong for this route.

contradictions.fact: Header/area elevation vs. this route's actual summit

claims.says: 8872 (Eldorado Peak / Main Peak)
elev 8113
TEPEH TOWERS IS NOT ON ELDORADO PEAK, despite being filed under the same area. It is a separate formation further along the icecap.

contradictions.why: The header shows the peak elevation from the area's elevation_ft (8872, Eldorado Peak's summit), but this route's own high_point_ft/summit waypoint and its own prose confirm its actual summit is a different, lower formation at 8,113 ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own fields (high_point_ft, waypoint, explicit prose) agree the true summit is 8,113 ft on a separate formation, not Eldorado's 8,872 ft.

contradictions.fact: Approach text describes the standard glacier route, not this route's crack/U-notch line

claims.says: From camp, the route continues onto glaciated terrain (roped travel and crevasse-rescue gear required) climbing toward Eldorado's famous narrow snow ridge and the 8,868-foot summit, typically another 3-5 hours. ... For this specific route: from Eldorado/Roush Creek high camp, continue up snowfields onto the Eldorado Glacier to the summit ridge system; West Ridge traverses further around past the Triad to the west face before ascending, but all three routes stay on Eldorado Peak itself.
Pitch 1 climbs an obvious crack up the face to the 'U-notch' on the ridge; pitch 2 follows excellent cracks on the far side; pitches 3-4 are classic exposed knife-edge ridge...
P1 (5.6 crack to U-notch), P2 (cracks), P3-P4 (knife-edge ridge), Summit scramble

contradictions.why: The approach field (largely shared boilerplate with the East Ridge route) describes ascending snowfields/glacier to the summit ridge system, never mentioning the crack-to-U-notch/knife-edge line that this route's own beta and pitch_detail describe as the actual climb; it also refers to a 'West Ridge' route, but no route named 'West Ridge' is filed on this peak (the rock route is named 'West Arete').
contradictions.internal_resolution: beta and pitch_detail (both specific to this route) describe the actual line; the approach field's route-specific paragraph does not match them.

contradictions.fact: Ridge crest grade: 5.7 vs 5.6

claims.says: note: Airy, exposed 5.6 ridge crest of solid granite to the summit.
Sources also disagree on the grade, 5.6 against 5.7, so do not read a hard move as evidence you are off route.

contradictions.why: The route's own headline grade fields (grade, rock_grade) both say 5.7, but a waypoint note on the same route states the ridge crest is 5.6 — a genuine disagreement, acknowledged in prose as a sourcing conflict but still presented as two different grade values on the same route.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own baseFinding text explains the 5.6/5.7 split as a real disagreement between sources rather than an error, but the displayed grade fields (5.7) and the waypoint note (5.6) still disagree.

contradictions.fact: Season window (Oct-Apr) vs. best_season/seasonal_guidance/seasonal_hazards, which describe a May-July season

claims.says: Oct-Apr

Highly conditions-dependent. Early season (roughly May-June) can offer steep, thin ice and moderate mixed climbing; by mid-to-late summer the couloir is usually mostly filled with snow and just a few ice steps; a good cold snap in early fall/winter (e.g., late October-November) can also bring in firm, well-bonded ice...
May: marginal, June: optimal, July: good
May: Considerable, June: Moderate, July: Low
Early summer holds good névé; later the couloir melts and opens.

contradictions.why: The route's own season field (Oct-Apr) excludes May, June and July entirely, yet best_season, seasonal_guidance's month-by-month breakdown, the avalanche-by-month table, and the climate notes all treat May-July (especially June) as the core/optimal climbing window.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The detailed seasonal_guidance/seasonal_hazards/best_season all agree the route is climbed May-July with June optimal; the terse season field (Oct-Apr) is the outlier.
